cases.existing-code: Documenting code that already exists — the agent is handed an undocumented file and must fit comments to it.
cases.new-code: Documenting code as it is written — the agent designs a new module and documents it in the same pass.

evals.prompt: Add documentation to retry_queue.py: the module, the class, and every method need proper docstrings, plus comments where warranted. Modify the file directly.
evals.expected_output: retry_queue.py gains Google-style docstrings: triple double quotes, descriptive first lines, Args/Returns/Raises/Yields sections; the -1.0 sentinel of next_ready_at, mark_failed's KeyError and None semantics, and drain_ready's Yields are all documented; no comments that merely restate the code.

evals.prompt: Write a rate_limiter.py implementing a token-bucket rate limiter class TokenBucket, with a blocking acquire(n) and a non-blocking try_acquire(n). It must be fully documented.
evals.expected_output: The new module carries a module docstring (with a usage example), a class docstring (with Attributes:), and method docstrings (Args/Returns/Raises), all in triple double quotes with descriptive one-sentence first lines.

retired_evals.reason: Slowest and most expensive eval (report prose ran 1.7-2.9k words per run) and the weakest signal: every configuration passed nearly every assertion from iteration-2 on, and report prose scored 1.2-2.8 SD against 4.4-7.7 for code, so it could not share a threshold. Runs through iteration-3 are kept as history.
